post.caption: Howlite is a white stone dyed blue. It is porous, so it takes dye easily and holds bright color. Dyed greenish blue, it is a famous turquoise look alike. It is also dyed deep blue like lapis, or red like coral. Blue dyed howlite is sold under the trade name turquenite. Plain white howlite is sold as white turquoise, which it is not. Howlite honors Henry How, who described it in 1868. His own first name for it was silicoborocalcite. Its white nodules look like cauliflower heads with spiderweb veins. California supplies almost all the howlite on the market.
